title: IMAGE RESIZER NOT WORKING
author: ravi
summary: The bare Image Resizer symptom has already been expanded into the richer installer root-cause issue #49992, which in turn tracks the current draft PR #49996.

judgment.rationale: Issue #49850 is now best understood as an application symptom of the mixed-version WinUI3Apps installer problem documented in #49992 and partially addressed by draft PR #49996.
evidence: The original issue provides only the bug-report ZIP as the reproduction artifact and later receives a maintainer comment saying it looks like an installer issue.
Issue #49992 explicitly states it was identified while investigating #49850 and its PowerToysReport ZIP.
Issue #49992 documents stale WinUI3Apps dependencies left behind after upgrade and names Image Resizer, Settings, and Peek crashes as observed consequences.
Draft PR #49996 replaces the custom hardlink/copy mechanism with MSI DuplicateFile authoring as part of that installer investigation.
judgment.recommended_action: Track the canonical installer issue and its draft PR instead of creating a separate Image Resizer-only design from this symptom report.

fix_assessment.rationale: The relevant concrete fix attempt is the active installer investigation and draft PR, not an Image Resizer-specific code change.

issue_context.summary: Image Resizer failed after upgrade, but the deeper investigation moved to a canonical installer issue about mixed-version WinUI3Apps dependencies.
known_information: The issue body contains a bug-report ZIP rather than a standalone Image Resizer repro narrative.
Maintainer moooyo commented that it looked like an installer issue and suggested reinstalling.
Issue #49992 was created from the investigation of this exact bug-report ZIP.
Draft PR #49996 is the current implementation attempt in that installer space.
inferences: The Image Resizer failure is a downstream symptom, not necessarily an Image Resizer code defect.
Any durable fix belongs in installer consistency/recovery logic so the affected WinUI utilities launch with matching dependencies.
issue_context.analysis: This issue should be represented as handled by canonical linked work. The dashboard artifact should not suggest an Image Resizer-local patch when the current evidence points at installer integrity.
initial_investigation: Issue #49992 records the mixed-version file list under WinUI3Apps and explicitly says neither it nor PR #49996 proves the entire #49850 symptom is solved yet.
PR #49996 is still draft, which means the right maintainer action is to monitor the installer fix path rather than open a second app-specific plan.
